relevance_note: Case series of children with A20 haploinsufficiency: "We describe four unrelated patients evaluated at a single tertiary center, each carrying a distinct TNFAIP3 mutation", with individual-level detail (sex, age, variant, phenotype, treatment) for each and for several relatives with HA20.
method_note: Read only the paper Markdown, the schema (schema_ha20_v5.json) and the rules; no other source, no web use. Every span was copied from the Markdown; the tricky characters were checked with regex searches against the file before writing, so the spans reproduce them exactly: the thin spaces U+2009 around '>' in the TNFAIP3 c.740C > T variant of A, the en dashes U+2013 in '3–4 weeks', '2–3 months', '1–2 ulcers', '3–4 years old' and '(17–21)', and the curly quotes around the case letters A–D. No script transcribed a table; Table 1 was read directly (it has no stacked ' / ' cells; its columns are Patient / Age of symptom onset / Sex / Main symptoms / Treatment / Outcome, and its patient labels A, B, C, D are used as the paper's own labels). Table 1 supplied sex, age of symptom onset and part of the symptom list for A–D. Uncertainties and decisions: (1) SCOPE OF RELATIVES - I gave a row to every relative the paper describes in relation to an in-scope person, including relatives it describes only as 'unaffected' (brother of A, mother of B, the two sisters of C, mother of D) and the second of the two brothers of B, who is described only by 'Neither brother has been genetically tested'. Those people have no phenotypic-feature rows, because 'unaffected' names no specific absent finding. If a stricter reading is wanted, these rows are the ones to drop. (2) The Discussion sentence 'Mutation p.Trp168* has been identified as pathogenic (ClinVar RCV005102078.1) (23) and identified in a patient with both HA20 and DLBCL, as found in the father of patient B (24)' is ambiguous: it may refer to the father of B or to a patient of reference 24. No separate person was created for it. (3) The 'mother and grandmother who were diagnosed with Behcet's' mentioned in the sentence about the ref (26) patient get no rows: the paper gives them no individual-level fact beyond that diagnosis. (4) is_proband is false for everyone, and that value has no span: the paper never calls any person a proband or index case, and this is a four-patient case series, so the 'single patient of a case report' clause does not apply. (5) cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is false with no span: the paper does not say that any of its patients were described earlier, and it only cites earlier literature for the variants. (6) vital_status is 'not reported' for the four patients: the paper never states that they are alive, though it describes ongoing care. It is 'deceased' only for the two aunts whose deaths it states. (7) VARIANT TYPE is recorded only for A (and for the previously published patient with p.Pro247Leu): the sentence 'Three out of four patients had non-sense mutations' and 'all three of our patients with non-sense mutations' name the group by the property asserted, so under D-29 the class is left 'not reported' for B, C and D. (8) The same logic applies to zygosity, which I took only from each patient's own sentence ('heterozygous mutation TNFAIP3 ...'). (9) B: the low absolute CD4 count was mapped to the checklist item 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' although the paper calls it neither cytopenia nor autoimmune. (10) B: 'biopsies were without clear celiac disease or inflammatory bowel disease' was recorded as excluded for celiac disease and for inflammatory bowel disease, but the broader checklist item 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' stays 'not reported' (a narrow absence does not exclude a broader item). (11) B and the ref (26) patient: the paper says 'fever', not 'recurrent fever'; the checklist item 'recurrent fever' was set to observed for them. (12) B: 'lymphoid aggregates in the duodenum' was kept as a feature but 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy' stays 'not reported'. (13) Negative findings were recorded as excluded rows naming the abnormality they rule out: 'normal chest x-ray (CXR) and electrocardiogram' (B) and 'His sinus and pulmonary computed tomography (CT) scans were normal.' (D); a normal investigation as a whole excludes nothing more specific, so no further item was excluded from them. (14) A: 'vaginal ulcers' (Table 1 and the case text) is the only genital finding, and the checklist item 'genital ulcers' was set to observed from it; 'anal ulcers' and 'nasal ulcers' are kept as stated features but not mapped to a checklist item. (15) D: the paper gives no stated age at the HA20 diagnosis (the diagnosis followed the admission at 13 years old), so age_at_diagnosis is 'not reported' for D; his age of symptom onset (9 years) comes from Table 1. (16) C: 'abdominal pain' is recorded as observed from 'Her abdominal pain has resolved'; her 'leg length discrepancy' was not mapped to 'growth failure'. (17) D: 'fatty liver' was not mapped to 'autoimmune hepatitis'; 'diverticulitis' (father of D) was not mapped to 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation'; the neurodevelopmental delay of the sister of A, the epilepsy and anxiety of the brother of D, and the thyroid cancer of the paternal grandfather of B were not mapped to any checklist item. (18) RELATIVES OF B/C: the second brother of B is labelled 'brother of B 2' and the second sister of C 'sister of C 2' under the relative rule, because the paper writes 'one of her two brothers' and 'Her two sisters' without separate labels or sexes for each. (19) The father of B is recorded as carrying B's variant: 'Her father has HA20 of the same genetic variant' is quoted together with B's variant string in his variant row, and no zygosity is given for him. (20) The three previously published patients (ref (15, 16), ref (2, 12, 22), ref (26)) each get a variant row because the paper ties the named variant to them; their variant strings are the protein strings the paper prints, since no cDNA is printed for them.
